summary: The clearest actionable signal is the Exhaustion Short panel: all 5 missed real moves (avg -5.82%) were blocked exclusively by the prev_day_rally gate, with actual values ranging from -6.21% to +3.81% against a hard 6% threshold — the gate is miscalibrated and needs to be relaxed or restructured with an OR-clause alternative. PDH Breakout is the most urgent triage case (0 wins from 21 signals, 17 losses) — the logic is firing on breakouts that immediately fail, pointing to a missing trend-quality filter rather than a threshold problem. The Trap Reversal panels and Momentum panels fire prolifically but win rarely, suggesting the core confirmation logic is insufficient, not just poorly tuned.

proposals.reasoning: All 5 missed real exhaustion moves (avg fall 5.82%) were blocked solely by prev_day_rally. Actual prev-day rally values were 3.81%, -0.41%, 1.75%, -0.87%, -6.21% — every single one was below the current 6.0% threshold. DRREDDY fell 5.75% after a -0.41% prior day; BANDHANBNK fell 7.32% after -0.87% and 5.72% after -6.21%. These are clearly multi-day exhaustion moves, not single-day blow-offs. The threshold of 6.0% is far too restrictive and filters out the most tradeable exhaustion patterns. Lowering to 2.5% captures all 5 missed signals while the cumul_rally OR-clause (already in the code) provides an independent safety net for stocks that haven't even rallied 2.5% in a day.
proposals.expected_impact: Recovers all 5 missed high-conviction exhaustion moves from the last 30 days. May increase signal count modestly; the other gates (impulse move, impulse turnover, same-slot volume, vol_ratio, nifty_chg) still filter noise.

proposals.panel: ORB — Opening Range Breakout (Bullish and Bearish)
proposals.reasoning: ORB Bullish: 0 wins, 1 loss, 7 expired from 8 signals (0% win rate, 87.5% expiry). ORB Bearish: 0 wins, 1 loss, 0 expired from 1 signal. The extreme expiry rate for the bullish panel (7/8 = 87.5%) indicates signals are firing on stocks that have a narrow opening range today but were actually moving around over the prior 3 days — a 5% high-low range over 3 days is a 1.67%/day average move, which is not a genuine compression setup for a stock priced above 100. Tightening to 3.5% (1.17%/day average) requires a more genuine multi-day contraction, reducing the number of signals on stocks that just happened to open narrowly by chance. Note: with only 8 and 1 total signals respectively, the 0% win rate is a small sample — the change is calibrated toward better setup quality rather than as a definitive response to the statistics.
proposals.expected_impact: Reduces ORB signal count, particularly cutting setups where the prior-days range was borderline wide. The 87.5% expiry rate suggests most current signals simply have no energy to break out — tighter consolidation requirement increases the probability that when a breakout does occur, it carries real pent-up energy.
proposals.skip_reason: LOW confidence — noted but not auto-applied

proposals.title: Replace AND with OR between prev_day_rally and cumul_rally gates
proposals.proposed_change: The current gate uses AND: BOTH prev_day_rally_pct < EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT AND cumul_rally_pct < EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT must be true to reject. Change the condition so a stock passes if EITHER prev_day_rally_pct >= EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT OR cumul_rally_pct >= EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT. Specifically, replace the gate block starting 'if prev_day_rally_pct < EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT and cumul_rally_pct < EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT:' with 'if prev_day_rally_pct < EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT and cumul_rally_pct < EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT:' — which is already an OR semantically at the pass side. The fix: invert to 'passes_rally = (prev_day_rally_pct >= EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT) or (cumul_rally_pct >= EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT); if not passes_rally: reject'. This is the intended logic the comment describes ('whichever is stronger') but the guard currently gates on BOTH failing. Suggested starting values: EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT=2.5, EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT=6.0 (existing cumulative threshold unchanged). Place this at the same position in the gate sequence.
proposals.reasoning: BANDHANBNK fell 7.32% on 2026-07-22 after a prev-day move of -0.87% and again 5.72% on 2026-07-23 after -6.21% — a two-day cumulative decline of ~7%, which is clearly a trending exhaustion scenario. DRREDDY had -0.41% prev-day but the cumulative context would have shown a prior run-up. The confidence scorer already uses max(prev_day_rally_pct, cumul_rally_pct/3.0), correctly treating them as alternatives — but the gate incorrectly requires both to pass simultaneously, so stocks with strong cumulative context but a weak or flat prior day get blocked before they ever reach scoring.
proposals.expected_impact: Catches multi-day trending exhaustion signals that currently only fail on a weak single-day prior move. Combined with the parameter_tune on EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT, this fully re-enables the 5 missed signals and aligns the gate logic with the scorer's intent.

proposals.title: Add ADR (Average Daily Range) quality filter to block low-quality breakouts
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new gate after the existing EMA and RSI filters: compute the Average Daily Range over the last 5 completed daily candles as a percentage of close — PDH_ADR_MIN_PCT = 1.5. If (avg of (High-Low)/Close * 100 over last 5 days) < PDH_ADR_MIN_PCT, reject the signal. This targets low-volatility stocks that technically satisfy the EMA and RSI filter but have been grinding up on thin daily ranges and lack the momentum to sustain a PDH breakout. Constant name: PDH_ADR_MIN_PCT = 1.5 (percent). Insert this gate immediately after the RSI gate and before the volume gate, as it only requires the daily batch already loaded. Additionally, add a gate requiring the breakout candle (the bar at bos_bar index) to close in the upper 50% of its own bar's range: breakout_bar_range = today_bars['High'].iloc[bos_bar] - today_bars['Low'].iloc[bos_bar]; if breakout_bar_range > 0 and (closes[bos_bar] - today_bars['Low'].iloc[bos_bar]) / breakout_bar_range < 0.5: reject. Constant name: PDH_BREAKOUT_CLOSE_THRESHOLD = 0.5.
proposals.reasoning: PDH Breakout has 0 wins from 21 signals and 17 losses over 30 days — an 81% loss rate. This is not a sample size issue (21 signals is substantial). The existing gates (EMA200, RSI>=60, volume>=8L) confirm trend and momentum on paper but do not check whether the breakout candle itself showed conviction. A bar that closes near its low after breaching PDH is a weak breakout that often fails immediately. Low-ADR stocks can have RSI 60+ and be above EMA200 simply by slowly grinding, yet have no real momentum for a breakout to follow through. With 17 pure losses (not expired, not noise), the current signal is worse than random; structural quality gates are the only credible fix.
proposals.expected_impact: Expected to significantly reduce signal count (filtering out the low-quality grinders) and cut the loss rate. Adds ~2 gates that require genuine breakout conviction. The panel may produce 0 signals on many days, which is preferable to 17 losses in 30 days.

proposals.panel: Bull Trap Reversal — Failed PDH Breakout (Bearish)
proposals.title: Require the trap bar to penetrate PDH by a minimum threshold before reversal is valid
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant TRAP_MIN_PENETRATION_PCT = 0.3. After identifying trap_bar (the first close above PDH for bull trap), require that the penetration was meaningful: penetration_pct = (closes[trap_bar] - pdh) / pdh * 100. If penetration_pct < TRAP_MIN_PENETRATION_PCT, reject with _dbg_fail(_debug, 'trap_penetration_too_shallow', symbol). Insert this gate immediately after the trap_bar identification block, before the reversal_bar search. Also raise TRAP_FRESHNESS_BARS from 6 to 4 for the bearish (Bull Trap) direction specifically — or add a separate constant TRAP_BULL_FRESHNESS_BARS = 4 checked when not bullish. Place the direction-specific freshness check at the same point as the existing TRAP_FRESHNESS_BARS check.
proposals.reasoning: Bull Trap Reversal (bearish) has 1 win, 6 losses, 12 expired from 19 signals — 5.3% win rate. The 12 expired signals (63% expiry rate) indicate the reversal is being called too early or on insufficient penetration — price re-crosses PDH briefly, gets flagged, but never actually falls. A trap requires a real false breakout: if the close only barely exceeds PDH by a few ticks, there is no trapped crowd to unwind. The high expiry rate (not loss — the signal just never moves) points to structural ambiguity at entry rather than directional error, which a minimum penetration gate would address. The TRAP_RECLAIM_MAX_BARS=12 gives 60 minutes for reversal which is reasonable; the freshness filter of 6 bars (30 min) may be allowing stale signals that already showed the trade had no follow-through.
proposals.expected_impact: Reduces the chronic expiry rate (12/19 = 63%) by requiring the false breakout to be real enough to trap meaningful size. Fewer signals but higher proportion of genuine setups. Bear Trap (bullish, 2W/1L/15E) has a different profile and is unaffected.

proposals.panel: Momentum Breakout — Range Open + Clean PDH Break (Bullish)
proposals.title: Add Nifty 50 alignment gate and require breakout candle to close above PDH by minimum margin
proposals.proposed_change: Two additions: (1) Add constant MB_BREAKOUT_MIN_MARGIN_PCT = 0.15. After identifying breakout_bar, require (closes[breakout_bar] - pdh) / pdh * 100 >= MB_BREAKOUT_MIN_MARGIN_PCT — the breakout candle must close at least 0.15% above PDH, not just tick above it. Reject with _dbg_fail(_debug, 'breakout_margin_too_thin', symbol) if not. Insert immediately after the breakout_bar identification loop. (2) Tighten the existing Nifty alignment check: currently nifty_chg < -1.0 blocks bearish-Nifty trades. Change to nifty_chg < -0.5 for bullish Momentum Breakout, since a breakout on a mildly weak market (-0.5% to -1.0%) is unlikely to follow through. Add constant MB_NIFTY_MIN_CHG = -0.5 for the bullish direction check.
proposals.reasoning: Momentum Breakout Bullish: 2 wins, 8 losses, 7 expired from 17 signals — 11.8% win rate. The current -1.0% Nifty threshold is the same as ORB and Trap panels; for a pure momentum continuation play that explicitly requires no gap and a PDH break, a market that's down even -0.6% is already fighting the premise. The margin gate addresses the same thin-breakout problem identified for PDH Breakout — a close of +0.02% above PDH satisfies the gate mathematically but has no conviction. Momentum Breakdown Bearish has twice as many signals (24 vs 17) and almost double the win rate (20.8% vs 11.8%), suggesting the bearish direction of the same logic works meaningfully better — likely because down-moves in Indian mid/small-caps are more impulsive. The bullish side needs stricter entry quality.
proposals.expected_impact: Reduces false breakout entries on thin closes above PDH. Tighter Nifty filter cuts signals on weak-market days where breakouts consistently fail. Should improve the 11.8% win rate at the cost of fewer signals, particularly filtering the 7 expired (non-directional) outcomes.
